scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.

A shared longitudinal narrative explicitly distinguishes colonial and independent Angola across the imported angola (1815 to 1878), angola-1900 (1900 to 1938) and angola-1960 (1960 onward) records. Their map gaps are not historical disappearances.

The 1815 and early 1900 polygons cover a coastal area; later snapshots approximate modern Angola. Countrywide heritage examples are not claims of Portuguese control over all such places in 1815. Modern territory is not projected backward onto the Kingdom of Kongo.
The imported People’s Republic of Angola alias does not make independence occur in 1960. The narrative dates independence explicitly to 1975 and leaves geometry unverified.

The Library of Congress volume was published in 1991 with research largely completed in 1989. Printed pages 18 to 21 and 137 to 138 were read. Its dated economic assessments are not current statistics, and colonial vocabulary or judgments are not adopted as the card’s voice.

The Ndembu nomination sections 1 and 3.2 were read, not every underlying manuscript. African-created records and the colonial outgoing-letter codex have distinct authorship. Conservation descriptions do not establish that every treatment was completed.

The slave-registration collection spans three countries. An official order to register people is not evidence of exhaustive compliance. Abolition of legal slavery is not presented as the end of coercive labor.

The Pwo catalog describes a specific Chokwe object from Xassenge. Its 2003 acquisition is distinct from its early twentieth-century manufacture. No original ceremony was observed and religious efficacy is not asserted.

Mbanza Kongo’s former kingdom and communities have histories distinct from the modern state. UNESCO inscription dates are recognitions, not founding dates. The catechism is not given an unsupported absolute first status.
Sona is attributed to Lunda Cokwe and neighboring peoples. The card uses the public inscription description; restricted ritual knowledge is not invented, and inscription is not an invention date.

The Alvor Agreement was checked against the official Portuguese publication. The Office of the Historian supplies context for its breakdown and the 1960s movements. Ethnic communities are not equated mechanically with political parties.
RTP’s written account and speech captions were consulted; the embedded films were not watched. Rival independence declarations are distinguished from a consensual transfer to one government.

The Luena text was read at chapter II and annex 4. It states commitments, while the November monitoring report provides a separate dated observation from indexed paragraph 5. The direct UN library PDF fetch returned 403; no full-document access is claimed.

The Luena settlement concerns government and UNITA forces and is not evidence that every conflict, including Cabinda, ended. Postwar periods identify selected developments rather than comprehensive political histories.
FAO is the implementing organization, so its outcome claims are attributed and confined to project areas. No source is treated as nationwide proof of eliminated poverty, drought or conflict.
Independent historical review, border assessment and depth certification remain pending.
